chunks: Rijal al-Kashshi: Hamduwayh, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from al-Husayn ibn Uthman, from Dharih who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying:

Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both) used to say: I dislike it for a man to be given good-health all his life in the Dunya and remain untouched by trials. Then he mentioned that Abu Sa'id al-Khudri was upright [on the true path]. He fell ill for three whole days so his family bathed him and carried him to his prayer-niche wherein he died.

key_terms.مُسْتَقِيمًا: upright, steadfast, or on the true path
key_terms.مُصَلَّاهُ: his place of prayer or prayer niche
key_terms.نَزَعَ: fell ill or was stricken with sickness
key_terms.يُعَافَى: to be given good health or freedom from illness

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn say about being free from trials in this world?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) conveys that Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them) preferred that a believer not be entirely exempt from worldly trials, as afflictions serve as spiritual purification and elevation. He illustrates this by citing Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, whose three days of illness were viewed not merely as suffering but as a means of steadfastness, culminating in his death within his place of prayer, signifying a blessed end.

en.ammaar-muslim: 1. [1/294] Rijal al-Kashshi: Hamduwayh from Ya’qub b. Yazid from Ibn Abi Umayr from al-Husayn b. Uthman from Dharih who said: I heard Aba Abdillah عليه السلام saying:

Ali b. al-Husayn عليهما السلام used to say: I dislike it for a man to be given good-health all his life in the Dunya and remain untouched by trials. Then he mentioned that Aba Sai’d al-Khudri was upright [on the true path]. He [Abu Sai’d] fell ill for three whole days so his family bathed him and carried him to his prayer-niche wherein he died.
